title: Chronicles of Avel - Review of base game and expansions
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UHGfFw-ZT98

Daniel (@dungeondive) makes the case for Chronicles of Avel, a family-weight co-op that looks like a kids' game, plays solo in 30 to 40 minutes, and is still available new on Amazon with both expansions. The game runs in two acts. Heroes explore hex tiles, fight monsters for coins, upgrade gear at the blacksmith, and buy castle walls, elf traps and portal seals; then the Beast crashes down and every monster marches on the castle in a tower-defence finale. What Daniel loves is the tangibility: chunky paper-doll character sheets where cardboard swords and helmets slot into place and flip to an upgraded side, a backpack you must physically fit potions and coins into, and gear drawn blind from a bag by feel in five seconds. Each piece adds coloured dice to your pool, and the power curve is genuinely felt. His complaints are small: two different icons for blocking, portals that too often land adjacent to each other, and no flavour text on the hexes. The $6 Adventurer's Toolkit should have been in the box, since it completes the armour set with boots. The New Adventures expansion is his favourite kind: modular Oberon and Titania merchants, cruel hunters, a Moon Beast whose powers shift every turn, and three linked scenarios with frog thieves, a wagon escort and moon machines.

----

Daniel suspects Avel's toy-like look pushes older hobbyists away. Have you been put off a good game by its family-friendly presentation, and what won you back?
